title: A shared definition or the passage's sense
statement: When a word's one course-wide definition does not fit the sense a later passage uses, should the lesson keep the shared definition or gloss that passage's own sense?
example: Restoring eight glossary definitions failed the one-definition check on two, and the course definition reused for one was narrower than the original gloss.
detail: A Grade 3 reading course's rules ask both for one definition of a taught word used exactly in every later mention, the passage glossary included, and for every hard passage word to get a definition in the sense used there. Restoring a design's eight glossary definitions failed the grade-wide consistency check on two words, and the course kept six verbatim and replaced two with its existing definitions, noting that equality alone does not prove a contextual sense is appropriate. For one word the shared definition is narrower than the original gloss and describes a plan the passage does not establish; the course recorded the swap as an editorial reuse, not a correction of the original gloss and not an academic ruling.
